awd_titl_txt: Conference: Intersections between criminal science and linguistics
awd_abstract_narration:
Language and language expertise have a role in the criminal legal system, whether it be through the interpretation and meaning of documents or testimonies, the treatment of the defendants, witnesses, and experts, or the processes through which juries and judges interpret and understand the evidence they are presented. Forensic linguistics, which focuses on criminal investigation, has had a significant impact, but other approaches in the scientific study of language generally have had less prominent engagement. This conference brings together language scientists who are working on issues in criminal science with lawyers and other social and behavioral scientists to explore and promote new lines of interdisciplinary research on language in criminal legal contexts to advance practice in the U.S. criminal justice system. This conference advances scientific domains at the intersection of linguistics, law and science, and other social and behavioral sciences. Other benefits to society include educational opportunities for students in addition to early career and established researchers.

The conference brings together experts and practitioners to identify current areas of successful collaboration and areas where linguistics can have greater impacts. Many experts contribute talks and panel sessions, and an open poster session showcases current empirical projects. The conference provides guidance and support to students and early career scholars with interests in addressing language in criminal legal contexts. The conference is co-located with a large, established gathering of language scientists to enhance the opportunity to advance work at this intersection, by hosting these activities in a setting that is accessible to a wide range of faculty and students.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
The conference, Advancing Criminal Justice Reforms through Linguistics, brought together linguists who are working on important issues in criminal justice with lawyers and other social and behavioral scientists to explore and promote how linguists can do more to help advance criminal justice in the United States. The conference was co-located at the Linguistic Society of America’s 2025 Summer Institute in Eugene, Oregon, which provided a key opportunity to advance work at this intersection with a particular impact on the field of linguistics, by hosting these important conversations in a setting that is accessible to a wide range of linguistics faculty and students.

The conference, held July 19-20, was designed with the primary goal of promoting dialogue and the sharing of research needs and activities, as well as creating networking opportunities to bring language/linguistic researchers together with legal professionals, with emphases on professional development opportunities for students and early-career researchers.

The conference included a plenary by Prof. John Baugh (Rice University), former LSA president, described important uses of linguistics in criminal law and explored the challenges of expert linguistic testimony in court. A detailed discussion followed regarding the appropriate limits of such expert linguistic testimony. A poster session was a primary site for sharing active research projects by students and faculty. And the conference featured sessions which included a mix of individual presentations, panel discussions, and audience-driven Q&A, each led by a subset of the invited participants, both legal experts and language scholars. The final sessions focused on more practical areas, with greater emphasis on career development for student trainees: the role of and opportunities for linguists as experts in legal cases and career and funding opportunities for linguistics students and researchers in these areas.

The conference effectively served its goals as a balance between knowledge sharing and the dissemination of ongoing efforts on the one hand, and research and career development. And the conference website provided a longer-term home for resources and materials to assist linguists interested in engaging with the legal system.

Major Activities:

Secure conference as an official weekend event at the 2025 Linguistic Society of America’s Summer Institute. 

Launch conference website.

Organizing and hosting conference, including panel sessions, plenary, and poster session. 

Specific Objectives:

All objectives were accomplished and completed. The conference was successfully hosted as part of the LSA's Summer Institute.  The conference website is: https://sites.google.com/view/linguisticsforjustice/home.

Significant Results:

To the organizer's knowledge, no other recent conferences have directly covered the topics this conference will address at the intersection of linguistics and criminal justice reform. We hope that the event promotes work at the intersection of linguists and the law.

Key outcomes:

Together legal professionals, linguists, and other social and behavioral scientists explored how research about language can advance criminal justice reform work. A wide range of basic issues in the social, economic, behavioral, and cognitive sciences were discussed, including: the role of language in biased decision-making, in (disparities in) the economic impacts of the criminal justice system, in the interpretation of legal texts and in legal argumentation, and language and prejudice. We believe that this conference had important intellectual impacts, advancing the breadth and depth of basic scientific inquiry into criminal justice outcomes by promoting greater communication and collaboration across disciplinary boundaries. 

The conference had direct impacts on the students and early career scholars who attended. We believe the conference made an intervention at an early enough stage to encourage up-and-coming scholars to engage in new work and to forge new interdisciplinary connections. By identifying and bringing together students and early career scholars with interest in these topics, the conference provided an opportunity to ask questions of and receive guidance and support from more senior scholars.

The conference’s sessions on linguists as experts and on opportunities in the criminal justice space and the broader discussions of the conference provided people interested in getting more involved in criminal justice applications or pursuing careers contiguous to linguistics with advice on how to appropriately move into these arenas.

Criminal justice is a key domain where interdisciplinary perspectives, theory making and testing, are most needed. Since convenings of linguists with legal professionals are rare, the conference represented a unique opportunity to increase convergence research in the social and behavioral sciences.

Finally, the conference website provides a resource, both for linguists interested in criminal justice related work and for lawyers looking for linguistic experts to consult. The conference website archives and hosts detailed information about the conference and participants.
